about: The English of 1750: every word both apps put on screen, in the manner of Samuel Johnson's Preface to the Dictionary as first printed in 1755. A shadow of copy/en.json, which holds the schema (surface, apps, example); a key missing here falls back to it. Spelling as test/data/en-x-1750.spelling.json; no stage-play archaisms, no capitalised common nouns, and the long s only in app.titlePage. Design: LANGUAGE.md section 6.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.text: about {boil} to boil, as experience has shewn

readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.text: It is how long this quantity of water has hitherto been in boiling, timed by your taps. For a quantity I have never timed, I reckon from the nearest I have. Tap It boils in earnest to-day, and I shall correct the time while the eggs are cooking.

readout.restored.text: I have taken up this one again after the page was reloaded. The times are true, but I cannot sound the alarm, so watch the clock.

refusal.whiteNeverSets.text: With the heat withdrawn, the water cools before the white is set. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.harderThanPan.text: With the heat withdrawn, this quantity of water ({water}) grows cool before the yolk arrives there. Firmest attainable: {limit}. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.counter.text: An egg left upon the table does not cease to cook because it has ceased to boil. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left softer.

refusal.tap.text: A cold tap cools the egg too slowly to arrest the yolk. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left a little softer.

refusal.unlikelySoft.text: The softest in which I hitherto succeed at least {hits} times in {of}: {limit}.

refusal.unlikelyHard.text: The firmest in which I hitherto succeed at least {hits} times in {of}: {limit}.

refusal.ice.text: Any shorter, and the white is yet raw. Softest attainable for this egg: {limit}.

action.hint.heating.more.text: Tap It boils in earnest when the whole surface heaves, and is not to be calmed by stirring; not at the first bubbles. I time the rest of the cook from your tap: a few seconds either way are of no moment, but a minute early is an errour. Until you tap, the countdown is but my conjecture.

controls.egg.more.text: A bigger egg takes longer, for the heat has further to go. One size upon the box comprehends very different weights; if therefore you have kitchen scales, weigh an egg, and give me its weight.

controls.measure.legend.text: Or measure it; any one suffices

controls.measure.hint.text: Kitchen scales are the most exact. Wanting them, wrap a slip of paper round the fattest part, and measure the slip.

controls.eggFrom.more.text: Eggs from the fridge are the most certain. A fridge is much the same from day to day and a room is not, and every degree moves the time a little.

controls.eggFrom.hint.text: I suppose {fridge} for a fridge and {room} for a room. Choose Your own if yours differ.

controls.start.more.text: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water at a full boil; they peel more easily. Cold water: the eggs in a cold pan, the fire lit, and tap It boils in earnest when the water rolls; the waiting for the boil included, they are done sooner. Sous-vide: I shall tell you when you ought to have begun, which is commonly some while ago.

controls.afterTheBoil.more.text: Keep it boiling: the water stays at a full boil till the eggs come out, and its quantity is of little moment. Fire out, lid on: the eggs once in boiling water, the water finishes them as it cools. This spares fewel; but the quantity of water decides the time, and too little cannot finish the work; measure it therefore.

controls.cooling.more.text: Out of the water, the yolk cooks on for some minutes. Iced water arrests it soonest, and so permits me to offer the softest yolks; a cold tap is nearly as good. Upon the table the egg scarcely cools; the softest yolks are therefore forbidden, and how much more the yolk will cook is not easily foretold.

controls.water.more.text: The quantity of water, the eggs not reckoned. It signifies most with the fire out, when the water's own heat cooks the eggs: more water stays hot longer. With the fire lit it signifies a little. I remember besides how long each quantity takes to boil; it is therefore worth measuring.

controls.eggsInPan.more.text: Cold eggs cool boiling water as they enter, and more eggs cool it more; so it is longer in returning to the boil, or, with the fire out, never returns. For eggs begun in cold water I have no need of it: your tap when the water boils already reckons them.

controls.altitude.more.text: The higher you are, the cooler water boils, and the slower eggs cook; upon a mountain, sensibly so. Tell me nearly how high you are, and I shall use the boiling point here shewn.

help.how.p1.text: I compute how heat passes into your egg, and how far the yolk and the white are set; and then I choose the time that leaves the yolk as you desired.

help.how.aside.text: I reason by [heat conduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation) through a sphere of the bigness of your egg, and the setting of white and yolk as a dose of heat accumulated over time, by the [Arrhenius equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhenius_equation). Every constant, with its authority, is in the [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#2-the-physical-model).

help.how.p2.text: The cooling is likewise to be counted. An egg taken from the water continues some minutes to cook from within; iced water stops it soonest, and the table scarcely retards it.

help.how.aside2.text: Upon the table, still air draws off heat so slowly, that the yolk ends within a fraction of a degree of where it would, had the egg never cooled at all. [README §5](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#5-carryover-the-cooling-step-is-part-of-the-recipe).

help.learn.p1.text: From your answers I learn how you like your yolk, and how your eggs cook; from your taps at the boil, how long your water is in boiling. A single reading of the probe teaches me how fast heat enters your eggs. No question is compulsory.

help.learn.aside.text: I use [sequential Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_filter) to learn your eggs and your taste, with an [ordered probit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_probit) for too rear, as was desired, and too hard. I keep every egg; so that when I am improved, I learn again from all of them. [The design](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer/blob/main/INFERENCE.md).

help.reliable.title.text: Of eggs to be relied upon

help.reliable.intro.text: The greatest help is to tell me how each egg came out; after that, all depends upon your manner of cooking.

help.reliable.forYou.text: For the eggs as now set out

help.reliable.every.text: Weigh the egg if you can: one size upon the box comprehends eggs that need very different times. Eggs straight from the fridge are more certain than eggs at the warmth of the room.

help.reliable.hot.text: Of all methods the easiest to perform rightly. Keep the water at a full boil the whole time.

help.reliable.cold.text: Tap It boils in earnest when the whole surface rolls, not at the first bubbles. That tap corrects my time while the eggs are cooking.

help.reliable.heatOff.text: The water does all the cooking; measure it therefore, and be liberal. With too little, the white will never set.

help.reliable.cooling.text: Iced water is the most certain, and a cold tap nearly as good. Upon the table the yolk cooks on; for soft eggs, therefore, use ice.

help.odds.p1.text: Under the time, I say which way an egg is likely to miss. The bracket under the slider shews where the yolk will probably fall, and grows narrower as I learn.

help.odds.aside.text: The bracket comprehends eight eggs in ten. When I choose the time, a white left unset is reckoned three times worse than a yolk a little too firm; I therefore incline somewhat to the longer side. The shading of the slider shews how often each degree comes out right for you.

help.unsure.counter.text: The table. No one appears to have made publick how fast an egg cools in still air, and that is therefore the weakest of my numbers.

help.unsure.heatOff.text: The fire out. I suppose an ordinary pan with its lid on; a heavy pot or a loose lid will alter the time.

help.unsure.white.text: Whites. I cannot distinguish a white that sets late from a cook who calls a tender white unset.

help.unsure.sousVide.text: Sous-vide. Below {floor} the white remains liquid and moves within the shell, which I leave out of my account; there I am not to be trusted. By my reckoning, so cool, the white takes hours, or even days, to set, if it sets at all.

help.sources.intro.text: The chief authorities behind my numbers. The [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#10-references) lists them all, with what each has settled.

help.source.williams.text: C. D. H. Williams, "The Science of Boiling an Egg", University of Exeter (1998). newton.ex.ac.uk/teaching/CDHW/egg (the host is gone; the page is in the Internet Archive)

help.source.buay.text: D. Buay, S. K. Foong, D. Kiang, L. Kuppan and V. H. Liew, "How long does it take to boil an egg? Revisited", European Journal of Physics 27, 119-131 (2006). doi:10.1088/0143-0807/27/1/013

help.source.abbasnezhad.text: B. Abbasnezhad, N. Hamdami, J.-Y. Monteau and H. Vatankhah, "Numerical modeling of heat transfer and pasteurizing value during thermal processing of intact egg", Food Science & Nutrition 4, 42-49 (2016). doi:10.1002/fsn3.257

help.source.denys.text: S. Denys, J. G. Pieters and K. Dewettinck, "Computational fluid dynamics analysis of combined conductive and convective heat transfer in model eggs", Journal of Food Engineering 63, 281-290 (2004). doi:10.1016/j.jfoodeng.2003.06.002

help.source.vega.text: C. Vega and R. Mercadé-Prieto, "Culinary Biophysics: on the Nature of the 6X °C Egg", Food Biophysics 6, 152-159 (2011). doi:10.1007/s11483-010-9200-1

help.source.weijers.text: M. Weijers, P. A. Barneveld, M. A. Cohen Stuart and R. W. Visschers, "Heat-induced denaturation and aggregation of ovalbumin at neutral pH described by irreversible first-order kinetics", Protein Science 12, 2693-2703 (2003). doi:10.1110/ps.03242803

help.source.hoyt.text: D. F. Hoyt, "Practical methods of estimating volume and fresh weight of bird eggs", The Auk 96, 73-77 (1979).

help.source.usda.text: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service, "High Altitude Cooking".

idle.welcome.text: This is our first egg together. I begin by reasoning from eggs in general; but as you tell me how each one came out, I learn to reason from yours.

controls.units.more.text: I begin with what is customary where your browser says you are.

controls.thermometer.more.text: When the counting-down of the cooling ends, the middle of the yolk is at its hottest, and I shall ask for one reading. Thrust the point to the very middle, and tell me the highest number you see: anywhere else, or any later, reads lower. That single reading teaches me how fast heat enters your eggs. Upon the table nothing is counted down, and I do not ask.

controls.thermometer.ask.text: Ask a reading after every egg

outcome.likely.firm.text: Probably as you desire; if not, a little firm.

outcome.likely.soft.text: Probably as you desire; if not, a little soft.

outcome.unsure.text: It may come out too soft or too firm; which, I cannot yet foretell.

outcome.miss.firm.text: It may miss; more likely too firm.

outcome.miss.soft.text: It may miss; more likely too soft.

outcome.whiteRunny.text: The white may yet be unset.

outcome.bracket.text: The bracket under the slider shews where your yolk will probably fall. To be secure against a soft yolk, slide to the right, till the left end of the bracket rests where you would be content; against a firm one, slide to the left, till its right end does.

outcome.why.text: Before your first egg I know neither your taste, nor your eggs, nor your kitchen, and the bracket therefore begins wide. Every egg you tell me of makes it narrower.

outcome.learning.text: To hasten my learning, answer both questions after every egg, and, having begun from cold water, tell me when the water boils in earnest. If you have a probe thermometer, a single reading instructs me most.

advice.toggle.text: How this may be made more certain

advice.fridge.text: Use eggs straight from the fridge: how cold a fridge is I know, but not your room.

advice.weigh.text: Weigh the egg. One size upon the box comprehends eggs that need very different times.

advice.ice.text: Cool the eggs in iced water. Upon the table, how much more the yolk will cook is not easily foretold.

advice.moreWater.text: Use more water. With the fire out, more water holds its heat longer, and small differences in its cooling signify less.

learned.literature.text: I have hitherto learned nothing. Tell me how each egg came out, and, having begun from cold water, when the water boils in earnest.

learned.pan.text: {water} of water is about {time} in boiling, as experience shews

learned.forget.more.text: I forget every egg you have told me of and every boil you have timed, and begin again from eggs in general. A wrong answer or two a few eggs more will wash out; this is for a new stove, a new kitchen, or a new beginning.

learned.confirm.message.text: I shall forget every egg and every boil, and the times return to where they began.

share.toggle.text: Send word how my eggs come out

share.what.text: I shall send how every egg was boiled and how you found it, those I already know among them. No name nor place: a number drawn at random upon this device stands for you. While this is on, I shall now and then move a time some seconds, to learn the faster.

share.more.text: One kitchen can teach me only of itself; many together shew me how eggs, pots, water and cooling truly differ, and the next version of the app begins every one from what they shewed. I send the egg's size, how it was boiled, the heat at which the water boils (which tells roughly how high you dwell), your answers, and what I expected. Moving a time some seconds teaches what the usual times cannot, and keeps within what you would call right. Leave off whenever you please; Expunge what I sent takes back every egg.

share.waiting.one: {eggs} more shall go when the server can be reached.
share.waiting.other: {eggs} more shall go when the server can be reached.

share.confirm.message.text: I shall bid the server expunge every egg this device has sent, and leave off sharing. What I have learned here remains.

share.deleting.text: Expunging. If the server cannot now be reached, I shall ask again until it answers.

share.deleted.text: Expunged: the server keeps nothing this device sent.

controls.language.more.text: English (1750) is English as Samuel Johnson wrote it. I change to it when you choose Imperial, and back when you choose Metrick. Should the reader find this stile tiresome, choose English: the modern tongue is restored, and Fahrenheit's scale kept.

controls.units.period.text: I can likewise write the imperial measures in the English of their day.
